source.title: Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal

teaching.hint: Which traversal tells you a subtree's root, and what does the other traversal tell you once that root is known?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A postorder suffix exposes a subtree root, while that root's inorder position divides its values into independent left and right intervals.
solution_outline.approach: Map each inorder value to its index. Consume postorder from right to left, recursively constructing an inorder interval; after taking its root, construct the right interval before the left interval.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: For each inorder interval, the next unconsumed reverse-postorder value is that interval's root, and the cursor advances once for every constructed node.
solution_outline.correctness: The root partitions an interval into exactly its left and right subtree values. Reverse postorder visits root, then right-subtree roots, then left-subtree roots, so building those intervals in that order consumes precisely their nodes. Induction on interval size yields both requested traversals.
solution_outline.complexity: The index map and construction each process n values once, for O(n) time and O(n) space including the map and worst-case recursion.
solution_outline.pitfall: Constructing the left subtree first while consuming postorder backward assigns right-subtree values to the wrong interval.

common_wrong_turns: Linearly searching inorder for every root
Building the left interval before the right when walking postorder backward
Assuming duplicate values can be located unambiguously
source_fidelity_notes: Examples and image were omitted; equal lengths, unique values, membership, validity guarantees, bounds, and tree-construction output were retained.
